metadata.title: Meta Makes New AI Bet on WhatsApp and Instagram

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is expanding its AI ambitions beyond chatbots by acquiring Swedish startup Stilla.ai to help agents complete transactions across WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram.
Axios reported that Stilla's team and technology will join Meta when the transaction closes. Founded in 2024, the company raised $5 million in pre-seed financing in January, underscoring how quickly Meta moved to absorb its capabilities.
The acquisition will support Meta Business Agent, a system designed to help companies interact with customers and facilitate transactions inside Meta's applications. The direct commercial goal is transforming conversations across its massive social platforms into purchases, bookings and other completed actions.
Meta Wants AI Agents to Produce Revenue
For Meta stock investors, the strategic appeal extends beyond adding another AI feature. If business agents can answer questions, recommend products and complete transactions without sending users elsewhere, Meta could make its apps more valuable to advertisers and merchants while strengthening its position in conversational commerce.
The purchase follows Meta's rollout of Muse, a personal AI agent built to perform tasks across applications and online services. Together, Muse and Business Agent suggest Meta is developing parallel assistants: one representing consumers and another helping businesses sell to them.
That model could deepen engagement and create new monetization opportunities across Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. It could also provide Meta with more signals about commercial intent, potentially improving advertising targeting and measurement.
Execution remains the challenge. Users and businesses must trust agents to interpret requests correctly, protect sensitive information and complete transactions reliably. Meta will also need to show that agent-driven commerce generates incremental revenue rather than simply shifting activity already happening inside its platforms.
Stilla's modest funding history makes this a small acquisition financially, but potentially meaningful strategically. Meta shares rose 6.2% Wednesday as investors assessed a broader AI push increasingly focused on agents that do things, not merely answer questions.
